items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009
items.q: Leroi Jones will talk about the Fairview Baptist Church

ctx.x: I’m assuming that they’re carrying on a tradition. But that could be an incorrect assumption.

No, no, of course it’s a tradition. You interviewed Wendell Brunious, one of the New Orleans musicians that’s — I showed you that picture of him when he was like six or seven years old standing there with his sister watching, well I guess it was the Olympia band, oh no, it might have been the Tuxedo. His father played in the Tuxedo band. So of course it’s a tradition. But it’s evolved a little bit. The marching bands of St. Augustine High School, that’s a coveted membership in this marching band. It’s a thing of…

with drumsticks and you can still see a high school kid walking down the street home from school with a sousaphone wrapped around his head. So you don’t see that every day in other cities. I know it’s not true. But I see it. I mean maybe I don’t see it every day but yeah, every day I can see some evidence that yeah, there is music here happening. Now do we want the paradigm to be the brass band playing funky music? I mean in some of these music programs we have whole marching bands and there is only a handful of…
